title: Course table maker and schedule maker FAQ.
lead: Short answers about this free timetable maker, UBC Workday Excel, waitlists, PNG export, and other-campus files (SFU, Waterloo).
a1: No. Parsing runs in the browser. Closing the tab does not send the file anywhere.
q2: Why is a lab missing from the grid?
a2: If the meeting pattern is blank, add a time first. Then you can place it on the timetable.
q3: How do Active, Waitlist, and Dropped look?
a3: Active uses a solid box, Waitlist a dashed box, Dropped a dotted box. Nothing is placed until you check it on the left.
a4: By unique course (subject + number + term). A lecture and its discussion do not double the credits.
q5: Can I edit an imported course?
a5: Yes. Editing updates the in-browser list only. The original Excel is never rewritten.
q6: Is this a timetable maker or a schedule maker?
a6: Both names fit. Timetable Craft is a free timetable maker and schedule maker: you build a weekly course table online, add classes, and export a PNG.
q7: Can I use this as a UBC course table maker?
a7: Yes. Import View My Courses Excel from UBC Workday, or add UBC classes by hand. That is the UBC timetable maker and UBC schedule maker path.
q8: Do I need a UBC Excel file?
a8: No. Add any class schedule manually. The UBC Workday import is optional.
q9: How do I get the Excel from Workday?
a9: Open Workday, go to View My Courses, then under that title click the first icon (the one to the left of the PDF icon). Import the downloaded .xlsx in Schedule Maker.
q10: Can you import SFU, Waterloo, or other school timetables?
a10: Not as a one-click import yet. Email a sample export from Quest, goSFU, ACORN, Minerva, or any campus portal and we will add the parser. You can still add those classes by hand today.
